newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk wants direct precious metal sales.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk wants direct precious metal sales.

text.p: Russia's financially-troubled Norilsk Nickel metals group wants to sell platinum, palladium and related metals directly to end-users and to start hedging operations in London, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"We currently sell metals to Almazjuvelirexport for 30 percent below world prices," Sergei Vetchinin said, referring to the state export agency.
"We are interested in selling ourselves, as part of our strategy of financial rejuvenation."
He said that RAO Norilsky Nickel's new first deputy general director, Yuri Kotlyar, would hold talks with the government on making Norilsk a so-called special exporter of precious metals.
Kotlyar was formerly acting director of the defunct State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones, or Komdragmet, where his brief included precious metals output.

Vetchinin said that Norilsk, Russia's largest producer of platinum, palladium, cobalt, nickel and copper, and a major supplier to world buyers, also wanted to widen its sphere of influence on international markets.
"We want to lessen our dependence on situations in London that are not always to our benefit," he said, referring to price falls that have hit Norilsk harder because it has not hedged.
He added that Norilsk's sole authorised exporter of non-precious metals, Interrosimpex, wanted to conduct hedging operations as well as sell more metals to U.S. and Asian markets.
Russia is one of the world's leading suppliers of platinum, palladium and related metals.
Vetchinin gave no details on Russian output or exports.
